edit.statement: A person can have more than one year of death.
edit.subject: died_in_year

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'died in year' functional, so that a person died in only one year?

Guillermo el Conquistador murió en 1087. ¿Descarta eso que también muriera en 1090?

Is it true that a person can have more than one year of death or that Abraham Lincoln was the first president of the United States?
propositional.side_fact: Abraham Lincoln was the first president of the United States.

derived.prompt: William the Conqueror died in 1087. Does that rule out William the Conqueror also having died in 1090?
chain: William the Conqueror died in 1087. (given in prompt)
A person can have more than one year of death. (edit)
So 1087 does not exclude 1090 as a year of his death: no, it is not ruled out.

derived.prompt: Charlemagne died in 814. Is it consistent with this fact that Charlemagne also died in 815?
chain: A person can have more than one year of death. (edit)
So dying in 815 as well is consistent with dying in 814: yes.

William the Conqueror died in 1087..why: True and settled: he died at Rouen on 9 September 1087.

sources.quote: He was taken to the priory of Saint Gervase at Rouen, where he died on 9 September 1087.

Charlemagne died in 814..why: True and settled: he died at Aachen on 28 January 814; hundreds of exact hits.

sources.quote: Charlemagne died in 814 and was buried at the Palatine Chapel (now part of Aachen Cathedral) in Aachen, his imperial capital city.
Magna Carta (Medieval Latin for "Great Charter"), sometimes spelled Magna Charta, is a royal charter of rights sealed by King John of England at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215.

Abraham Lincoln was the first president.why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: Lincoln was the 16th president; Washington was the first.

sources.quote: Abraham Lincoln (February 12, 1809 – April 15, 1865) was the 16th president of the United States, from 1861 until his assassination in 1865.

notes: RBox revision of the topic's functional slot: 'died in year' loses functionality (axiom ¬Func), stated positively ('A person can have more than one year of death') so the negation has no stacked negative. The direct question asks the property by name with its meaning spelled out, since the bare 'Can a person have died in more than one year?' was answered 'yes' by all 4 models before any edit. Functionality holds without exception: a person dies once, and both instances are settled (William I, 9 September 1087; Charlemagne, 28 January 814). The first instance asks whether one year rules out another (yes before, no after) and carries the cross-lingual queries; the second asks whether a second year is consistent (no before, yes after). Near unrelated asks functionality of another history relation ('ended in year', yes). Far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. Caveat: the edit overrides what death means, not just a relation tag; worth tagging for slicing. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
